name: The Adubi war

summary.text: In 1918 Britain brought direct taxes, on top of forced labour and fees, to Egbaland, which had kept its own government until 1914. On 7 June the British arrested 70 Egba chiefs. About 30,000 rebels rose, tore up the railway at Agbesi and derailed a train, burned the station at Wasinmi, and killed a European agent and the Osile of Oke-Ona, David Sokunbi Karunwi II. For three weeks they fought colonial troops, many of them just back from East Africa, at Otite, Tappona, Mokoloki and Lalako. By 10 July the rising was crushed. About 600 people died, Abeokuta’s independence was abolished, and the direct tax was postponed until 1925.

moments.title: Seventy chiefs arrested
moments.text: The British arrest 70 Egba chiefs and order the resisters to lay down their arms and pay the tax.

moments.title: The railway torn up
moments.text: Rebels pull up the line at Agbesi and derail a train, demolish Wasinmi station, and kill the Osile and a British agent.

moments.title: Three weeks of fighting
moments.text: Colonial troops fight the rebels at Otite, Tappona, Mokoloki and Lalako. Leaders are killed or arrested; about 600 die.

reviewNotes: Agbesi, Otite, Tappona, Mokoloki and Lalako are not located; the fighting is drawn approximately south of Abeokuta.
